_comment: W1-T3323 MIGRATION AUDIT, not a live baseline. Frozen from CLAUDE.md at 888b2ffa1 -- the commit BEFORE the bodies moved to doctrine/. Each row is one rule as it stood pre-migration: its headline verbatim, and the sha256 plus byte length of its body. test/the-doctrine-index-points-at-every-body.test.ts re-derives both from the LIVE index+store and requires an exact match, which is what proves the move was a MOVE and not a rewrite. A digest, not the prose itself, because a second copy of 34KB of doctrine in the tree would answer every `git grep` for a rule phrase twice and quietly break the several suites that count those hits. EDITING A ROW HERE IS A DELIBERATE ACT: it means a rule body legitimately changed, and the diff should say why.

rules.headline: Run the shipped local gate before your FIRST push, not every commit.

A test run with no `# tests` summary is NOT A RESULT, and a summary over an UNVERIFIED FILE LIST
  is not one either — `node --test` given a ghost path returns a green count, silently. `ls` first.

THE BLOCK MUST PARSE BEFORE ANY PROOF IN IT CAN RUN — check GITHUB'S STORED BODY with
  `rmd check-acceptance`, never your local file.

EVERY proof needs a dialect prefix — `unit test:` or `grep:`. A bare title is PROSE and never
  executes.

A `unit test:` title is matched as a LITERAL substring after escaping — the OPPOSITE of a
  `grep:` pattern, which is a BASIC REGEX.

Require a verbatim `grep -rlF -- '<substring>' test/` hit — a passing scoped test run is NOT
  evidence the proof resolves.

Verify a `grep:` proof with the executor's REAL invocation — `grep -arn -- '<pattern>' <path>` —
  never with `grep -F`.

A `grep:` proof must match text on ONE PHYSICAL LINE — a YAML block scalar wraps, and the
  pattern then reads 0 at head with no error.

A new `.ts` file's `DA:<line>,0` on a doc comment or `interface` body is EXEMPT — never reorder
  a file to dodge it.
rules.refrozenReason: RENAMED AND REWRITTEN because the gate it described stopped behaving that way. The old form told authors to sandwich type-only declarations between covered functions, citing #777. W1-T171 later added computeTypeOnlyRanges to diff-coverage, which exempts every interface member line by brace context, and isNonExecutableLine already exempted leading doc comments. MEASURED 2026-09-11 on src/lib/ledger-compaction-rung.ts: all five head-placed interface member lines read DA:...,0 in the lcov AND return typeOnly=true from the live function. Obeying the stale form cost a reordering that was reverted in the same branch. This is the one legitimate reason to touch a frozen row: the rule changed, not the migration.

rules.headline:
When every test injects a fake, the seam's DEFAULT implementation and each `catch` arm are
  unreachable — write one test that really shells out, and one per catch arm.

Before trusting `diff-coverage: OK`, prove the lcov INSTRUMENTS the changed files —
  `grep -c '^SF:<path>$' <lcov>` must be non-zero for every source file in the diff.

Build the lcov and the diff from the SAME tree — commit before measuring — AND NAME THE SHA in
  what you report.

`diff-coverage` flags ADDED lines, so restructuring an untested region inherits its debt at the
  gate — measure MAIN's coverage of that region before assuming the PR caused it.

A deps object supplying SOME fakes leaves every other seam on its REAL default — so relaxing a
  guard can make a previously-dead default FIRE, in a file the diff never touched.

Verify a new falsifier by DELETING the fix and re-running — `# fail N` removed vs `# fail 0`
  restored is the evidence it is load-bearing.

ZERO A `DA:` VALUE INSIDE THE TARGET's OWN `SF:` BLOCK — a whole-file replace hits another
  file's identical line number and returns a FALSE `OK`.

Derive "which tasks are merged" from the `Remudero-Task:` trailer on merged PRs — never from
  ledger verdict lines.

AND A TRAILER-ONLY SET UNDER-CREDITS, because the BRANCH NAME is a second, independent credit
  path.
THE TWO SCOPE-TIME CHECKS, AS COMMANDS — RUN BOTH BEFORE BUILDING A FILED TASK.
Sweep the SUBJECT over open PR heads, not only `origin/main` — the id half already does.
NAME A SESSION BRANCH `run-<taskId>-<epochMs>` WHEN BUILDING A FILED TASK.

Before believing "task X is next", confirm the frontier with the repo's own selector —
  `runnableCandidates(plan, isMerged, n)` — not the task a brief or retro names

A contested reservation is never deleted and an unfiled one is never free — the
  LOSER of a race renumbers.

`rule15-filing` refuses a plan record in `files:` only when an OUT-OF-PLAN path rides along —
  the record ALONE passes at `verify: auto`.

A shard's `status:` field is not a completion signal — it stays `queued` on tasks that
  shipped.
Decoding rule citations — where each family canonically lives.
Do NOT push a fresh sha to clear a stale-red `ci-gate` — it self-clears.
CADENCE IS THE BUDGET, NOT INTENT — a sparse check-in is fine, a poll is not. NOW ENFORCED:
`gh pr create` may die on API quota; git push is unaffected.

A CONFLICTING PR registers ZERO check runs. `total: 0` reads as "still queued" but means
  `mergeable_state: dirty` — check mergeability before waiting on CI.

When two PRs append tests to the same file's TAIL, the conflict region can cut just before a
  SHARED closing `});`

A corrected PR title is observed by a RE-RUN, not only by a new sha — but `edited` still fires
  nothing.

A merge to a BAKED path ships nothing until an operator triggers an image rebuild — know which
  half of your diff you are in before you call a merge "shipped."

The rotations come in TWO FORMS and every glob that names only one answers SILENTLY WRONG. The
  union is three patterns, never two:
THE CONTROL MUST PROVE EACH FORM WAS READ, and a raw cross-archive count CANNOT
And the archives are NOT cumulative snapshots.
A ledger line must carry the reason from the DECISION THAT PRODUCED ITS OUTCOME.

On a zero match, `node --test --test-name-pattern` still emits `ok 1 - <RELATIVE test path>` —
  exclude the wrapper by the RELATIVE path, never the absolute one.

A fixture shelling git PLUMBING fails on every CI runner and passes on every dev machine, so it
  reads as flaky when it is deterministic.

When a gate reads the ledger for a record the SAME function writes, check the WRITE ORDER before
  believing the gate's stated reason.
`rmd drain --dry-run` is neither side-effect-free nor able to see your branch.

A bound that fires on a HEALTHY condition is this repo's recurring defect — before tuning the
  number, check the population it is meant to separate has ever been observed.

A ZERO IS NOT A MEASUREMENT UNTIL A POSITIVE CONTROL PROVES THE QUERY COULD SEE ITS CORPUS.
  RUN ONE ON EVERY SWEEP WHOSE ANSWER YOU INTEND TO ACT ON.

(a) A POSIX REGEX ENGINE HERE SILENTLY DROPS `\s`/`\b` INSTEAD OF ERRORING, AND TWO DIFFERENT
  TOOLS DO IT.

(b) THE `grep` IN THIS HARNESS IS A ugrep WRAPPER WITH `-I` (ignore-binary) INJECTED, so a file
  holding ONE NUL byte is skipped entirely — no output, exit 1, indistinguishable from real
  absence.
(c) A GLOB THAT NAMES ONE FILE FORM ANSWERS FROM THE OTHER WITHOUT SAYING SO.

(d) A QUERY CAN ANSWER THE WRONG QUESTION WITH A PERFECTLY GOOD ZERO, AND NO POSITIVE CONTROL
  SAVES YOU.

(e) A CONTROL PROVES THE QUERY CAN SEE ITS CORPUS; IT DOES NOT PROVE THE CORPUS IS THE RIGHT ONE
  — AND RE-RUNNING THE SAME WAY IS NOT A SECOND OPINION.

(f) THE TWO SIDES OF A COMPARISON MUST COUNT THE SAME UNITS — `ls` COUNTS A DIRECTORY AS ONE
  ENTRY.

(g) A CHANGE THAT REMOVES AN ACCESS PATH MUST PROVE THE REPLACEMENT FIRST, FROM A NEW SESSION
  — AN EXISTING CONNECTION IS NOT EVIDENCE.

(h) A GATE RUN FROM A CHECKOUT that is BEHIND answers about a file and a threshold that both
  moved — run it against `origin/main`'s blobs and report the behind-count.

(i) A POSITIVE CONTROL PROVES THE QUERY CAN SEE ITS CORPUS; IT DOES NOT PROVE THE CORPUS COVERS THE
  WINDOW.
(j) A CENSUS TEST NAMES NONE OF YOUR SYMBOLS, SO THE CALLER SWEEP ABOVE CANNOT FIND IT
(k) A RULE 21 protocol run passing `{ baseTask }` ALONE reports THREE INDISTINGUISHABLE ZEROS.

Read re-entrancy from `process.env`, not an injected `env` argument — a spawn writes a child's
  environment and cannot reach a parameter.

A fixed date constant compared against rows stamped at REAL time is a time bomb; the signature
  is a red beginning at a clock boundary with no diff involved.
